newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mun Loong sees over 5 mln rgt year net.
newsitem.headline: Mun Loong sees over 5 mln rgt year net.

text.p: Mun Loong Bhd president and chief executive Nor Mohamed Yakcop said on Monday that the company is expected to post over five million ringgit in net profits for the year ending in March 1997.
For the previous full year, the company had a loss of 8.47 million ringgit.
"It should be over five million for the whole year," Nor Mohamed said at a news conference, when asked for a profit projection. He said the figure represents the company's expected net profit.
He also announced that Mun Loong has been awarded three construction projects valued at 145 million ringgit.

The first, for which Mun Loong has been awarded a turnkey contract, is to build luxury villas on an island 15 km east of Phuket in Thailand. The project is worth 120 million ringgit for the first phase, Nor Mohamed said.
Over five years' time, the Thailand project would be valued at 600 million ringgit, he said.

The second contract involves an award worth 15 million ringgit to construct a medical centre in a Kuala Lumpur suburb, while the third involves construction of a club house worth 10 million ringgit in the northern state of Perak.
Diversified retail and construction firm Mun Loong's stock was suspended on Monday pending news of the projects. The stock closed at 15.60 ringgit on Friday.
Retail currently contributes 100 percent of the company's net profit, but Nor Mohamed said the company expects that segment's contribution to be not more than 20 percent at the end of three years.
By the 1997 financial year, he said the company expects construction to make up 60 percent of net profit and retail to contribute 40 percent.
